title: Generic declaration inventory lacks reflective typed invocation
observed_need: Bind an authoritative compiler callable identity to a bounded typed invocation without generating consumer-specific dispatch source.
current_language_behavior: mncs declaration-inventory exposes declaration, callable, test-case, source, profile, signature, effect, and capability identities. MNCS application code cannot yet invoke an arbitrary heterogeneous callable by that identity.
why_insufficient: provider.mncs must consume a static generated typed binding for the seven self-suite tests; removing the generator would replace explicit glue with hidden host dispatch policy.
minimal_reproducer: tools/generate_provider.py consumes mncs declaration-inventory and emits native/mncs/test/provider_inventory.mncs; a generic callable identity plus typed argument material has no native invocation boundary.
desired_direction: A generic exported-callable binding and typed invocation capability with signature validation, identity admission, and fail-closed mismatch behavior.
workaround: Keep deterministic source generation as a thin compiler-inventory-bound adapter. It may enumerate and encode signatures but cannot add tests, evaluate assertions, or aggregate results.
